newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ Dec qtr retail sales static - Statistics NZ.
newsitem.headline: NZ Dec qtr retail sales static - Statistics NZ.

text.p: After adjusting for seasonal effects and price inflation, New Zealand retail sales were estimated to have fallen 0.1 percent in the December 1996 quarter, Statistics New Zealand said on Monday.
"There was an increase of just 0.1 percent in the underlying trend in retail sales," SNZ said.
Actual retail sales rose by 2.5 percent or NZ$252 million from the December 1995 quarter to reach $10.4 billion in the December 1996 quarter.
The food storetype contributed $131 million, or 52 percent, to the total annual increase in actual retail sales.
Other storetypes to record significant annual dollar increases in actual retail sales were recreational goods outlets, up $45 million, and accommodation, hotel and liquor outlets, up $38 million.
SNZ said the North Island recorded an increase in retail sales of 2.7 percent between the December 1995 and December 1996 quarters, and the South Island recorded an increase of 1.7 percent.
Retail stock levels rose 0.9 percent from the end of the December 1995 quarter to the end of the December 1996 quarter.
Actual retail sales for the month of December 1996 reached $3.84 billion, an increase of 1.6 percent from the December 1995 month.
Actual retail sales rose 3.7 percent in the year ended December 1996 when compared to the December 1995 year, SNZ said.
